notes.title: 🚩 Checkpoint Mode! 🚩
notes.notes:
[p]After a lot of work and listening to the community, I’m excited to introduce the brand-new [b]Checkpoint Mode[/b]![/p][p]
Your progress will now automatically save at the flags you find on the map. [/p][p]This means you won’t have to start over from the beginning every time you fall, you’ll restart from the last checkpoint you reached.[/p][p]
This mode is designed to make the game more accessible without losing the intense challenge and sense of achievement you love.[/p][p][/p][p][b]You can find Checkpoint Mode in the MAIN MENU.[/b][/p][p]
Try it now, share your experience, and help me improve the game with your feedback!
[b]Thanks for the support and keep climbing to the top![/b][/p]

[b]1,000 players on One Box One Goal! [/b]

As a solo developer, this is beyond anything I could have imagined. Every single one of you who has downloaded, played, shared feedback, and supported this project has made this dream come true. When I started, it was just me, some code, and a lot of late nights, but seeing the community grow and hit 1,000 players fills me with so much gratitude and excitement for what’s next.

This game exists because of you. Your support has driven me to push through challenges, continue improving, and keep adding new features. Whether you’ve been here since day one or just joined, I appreciate each and every one of you.

[b]I'm currently working very hard on a multiplayer mode, something many of you have been asking for! It’s a huge project, but I’m dedicated to making it as awesome as possible, and I hope to have it ready soon. I can’t wait to share this new experience with all of you![/b]

From the bottom of my heart, thank you for being part of this journey. Here’s to many more milestones together! 


Stay tuned, as i said, there’s a lot more to come! 👀

- Max

notes.title: NEW UPDATE
notes.notes:
I’ve added [b]small but helpful safe zones[/b] above the map to make your journey a bit less punishing. These zones will slightly reduce the chance of falling all the way back to 0 meters, giving you a little extra chance to recover. However, don’t expect them to be huge, these safe zones are designed to offer just a small window of help, not a free ride!

[b]🤔 Difference Between 2D Getting Over It and my game:[/b]
The main difference between the 2D and my version of the game is the perspective and the complexity of movement. In 3D, the world feels much more dynamic, giving you a broader view and more freedom to explore. But this also makes it harder to control the hammer precisely, with depth and angles adding a whole new layer of challenge. It’s a different experience, one that tests your patience and skills in a way that feels both rewarding and frustrating.

[b]❓ Why sometimes i sent back all the way down?[/b]
One thing to note about the 3D version: it's not possible to add as many safe zones underneath as Bennett Foddy did in the 2D version. In 3D, you can fall in any direction, and even a small mistake could send you flying too high, potentially skipping past the safe zones altogether. The complexity of movement means there’s more room for error, but also more room for you to [b]improve with practice[/b].

[b]This game is all about patience.[/b],  is not for everyone. It’s designed for those who have patience and persistence, as it will test both. Every fall, every setback, is part of the process. If you’re not ready for this challenge, it’s best to step back. But if you’re determined and willing to put in the time, you’ll improve with every try. 

[b]With enough practice, you’ll learn to control the hammer more fluidly, and soon you’ll be swinging it as effortlessly as a gymnast flipping through the air.[/b]

[b]Stay patient, keep practicing, and don’t give up, you’ll improve with every try!
[/b]

Lastly, the game [b]is not designed to be played with a gamepad[/b], you can use it, but you may run into issues. [b]Gamepad support will improve with updates[/b], for the best experience, use a mouse and keyboard. <3

notes.title: AVAILABLE NOW!
notes.notes:
One Box One Goal is available now!

The challenge you've been waiting for is here! One Box, One Goal, a 3D adventure inspired by the challenging world of Getting Over It, is now live on Steam!

Navigate through mind-bending obstacles, test your patience, and conquer your way to victory, all while controlling a box with a singular goal: reaching the top. It's time to rise to the challenge and prove you’ve got what it takes.

Get it now and see if you have the skills to overcome the ultimate test of perseverance!

notes.title: 🚀 RELEASE DATE! 📦🏔️
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

I’m beyond excited (and honestly a little nervous) to finally announce that [b]One Box One Goa[/b]l is [b]releasing on February 17[[/b] on Steam! This game has been a huge project for me, and if you love games like Getting Over It, then you’re in for a wild ride, except this time, in [b]3D.[/b]

[b]🎮 What’s One Box One Goal?[/b]
It’s a rage-inducing, skill-based climbing game where you control a character inside a cardboard box, using a hammer to navigate the 3D environment. Every movement matters, every mistake can send you plummeting back down. It’s tough, frustrating, and (hopefully) rewarding, just the way these games should be.

[b]🔥 What to Expect:[/b]
A true test of patience and precision (you will fall, a lot).
A fully 3D world with tricky terrain and vertical challenges.
Perfect for streaming, speedrunning, and suffering with friends.
No checkpoints, no hand-holding, just pure determination.
Leaderboards.
I’d love for you to check it out, add it to your wishlist, and maybe even share it with a friend who enjoys a good challenge. This game is my take on the genre, and I can’t wait to see how far you can make it!

See you at the top... or at the bottom. 😈
